claims.claim: The ownership manifest still validates after the change: 7 bots, 90 rules, no duplicate patterns.

G-1 passes for bot-00-programming-lead on every path this branch touches. The two new paths resolve to bot-00 through the existing docs/vps-agent-bus.md and skills/agent-bus/** rules, so no rule dangles and no path is unowned.
G-3 reports no secret in the three changed non-receipt files. No bus token, wss credential, or API key was written.

Both files name the four live agent_bus_* tools, keep the skill frontmatter shape the pack uses, record that stdio user-hermes stays uninstalled and hermes-mcp-bridge.mjs is not rebuilt, state the GitHub draft PR as the durable output, and contain no credential literal.
ownership.yaml is unchanged from origin/main — the manifest already matched both new paths, so nothing needed editing there.

The diff against origin/main on the complete branch is four paths — skills/agent-bus/SKILL.md, docs/vps-agent-bus.md, docs/intake-e2e-runbook.md, and this receipt — all owned by bot-00. The earlier wording named only the first three because the evidence command had been run before the receipt was committed.
G-2 fails closed on this receipt while approved_by is empty. That empty field is intentional — LEAD does not self-approve. It is not a completed approval and not a passing gate.

Greptile round 1 on PR #14 raised one P1 and four P2. Four were valid and are fixed in this branch: the P1 lost-jobId gap (the skill now writes the jobId to the receipt the moment agent_bus_start_job returns, since the step-2 idempotency check reads jobIds from .receipts/ and a session-only jobId is an invisible running job); the P2 idempotency_key overclaim (both files now state server-side dedup is unverified, matching docs/intake-e2e-runbook.md, which already declined to claim it); the P2 stale changed-file claim in this receipt; and the P2 runbook self-contradiction. G-1 and G-3 still pass on all four paths after the fixes.
No secret was introduced by the Greptile round. G-3 passes on the complete four-path branch.

The extended content assertions pass: the jobId-before-waiting rule is present in both files, neither presents idempotency_key as retry protection, and agent_bus_wait_job now uses the live descriptor's timeout_sec and poll_sec names instead of the looser 'timeout default 180s' phrasing.

The runbook no longer contradicts itself about these two paths. Greptile cited line 146; four further places said the same thing (the BUS_TOKEN paragraph, both ownership-table rows, and the unverified list) and all five are corrected, so no surviving line tells an operator the skill is absent.
